status_note: Still open on main (a4d8e00342d0): [`functions_arithmetic.yaml` L1492-L1516](https://github.com/substrait-io/substrait/blob/a4d8e00342d0/extensions/functions_arithmetic.yaml#L1492-L1516) says only that `corr` of no input is null, and [`functions_arithmetic.yaml` L1394-L1491](https://github.com/substrait-io/substrait/blob/a4d8e00342d0/extensions/functions_arithmetic.yaml#L1394-L1491) (`std_dev`, `variance`) say nothing beyond their names; no option or sentence covers one pair, a constant side, or `±inf`/NaN input. No existing issue.
summary: `corr` says what no input gives (null); `variance` and `std_dev` say nothing about it, though they return nullable types. None of them says anything about the degenerate cases: `corr` of one pair or of a side whose values are all equal, and any of them over a group with `±inf` or NaN. Engines give NULL or NaN there.
repro: DuckDB 2.0 and Polars 2.1: NaN for both; Spark 4.3: NULL for both. DuckDB: `var_samp` over `[inf, 1]` is NaN.
handling: The core allows NULL, NaN or a raise (`stat_degenerate`); the reference gives NULL for `corr`, as the SQL standard does, and raises for an infinite value. `semantics="duckdb"` gives NaN.
Could be expressed as: An option, such as `on_degenerate: [NULL, NAN]` and the existing `on_domain_error` for non-finite input, or a sentence in each description.
